speakers: Mark rinsky (guest, Systematic Investor co-host, rules-based investor)
summary: Weekly trend-following chat (July 2024): Treasury bill issuance as offset to QT, trend giveback and calm-regime risk, market add/drop rules, how to read backtests and build systems, stock-bond correlation, GIC/JPM paper placing trend following as loss mitigation, caution on LLM/ML, and law of small numbers.

coverage.note: Treasury bill issuance offsets Fed (Hudson Bay paper)
issuance rule of thumb, trend giveback, calm regimes
cost of crisis alpha, July 2024 trend performance
market selection criteria, vol floors, cocoa
cocoa, vol targeting in pegs, backtest value
three components of a system, simple rules, risk management
Stocks Crisis and False Alarms; prices as null
price action vs data; LLM and ML caveats
tech revolutions, public to private information

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: the activist treasury issuance of more more bills than coupons has had an impact of providing quantitative uh easing that's offset what the FED has been doing
claims.claim: Heavy Treasury bill issuance relative to coupons acts as de facto QE that offsets Fed tightening, which helps explain strong US growth, slow disinflation and easy financial conditions.
claims.indicator: bill vs coupon issuance share (Hudson Bay paper)
claims.direction: easier financial conditions, lower long yields
claims.conditions: while Treasury skews issuance to bills
claims.testable: yes: Treasury issuance composition is public

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: so if you issue more uh bills it's as if you're issuing more money
claims.claim: Bills are near-money and usable as collateral, so more bills adds money-like assets, while fewer coupons makes risky long-duration supply scarcer and lowers long-term rates.
claims.indicator: bill share of issuance; coupon supply
claims.direction: long yields down when coupon supply falls
claims.testable: partly: transmission channel hard to isolate

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: there's a greater demand for treasury bills because of the way we've changed the regulations on U money market funds that came around in 2016
claims.claim: The 2016 money market fund rules raised structural demand for short-term instruments, so Treasury has room to issue more bills.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: we'll do about 15% in bills and the rest in coupons they've done numbers that are much higher on the on the bill side
claims.claim: Treasury's rule of thumb is about 15% bills, but actual issuance has been much higher, shifting supply versus demand along the curve.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: somewhat Relentless giveback of performance that Trend followers have experienced in the past three months and actually it continued in July
claims.claim: Trend followers gave back performance for three months through July 2024, which strains investor conversations but may open entry points.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: might have a bit of a struggle like they had in the uh the 10 years uh leading into 2019 where everything was well controlled by central banks
claims.claim: If macro calms again (inflation and rates controlled), trend followers may struggle as in the decade to 2019.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it also opens up for some great entry points because still around you know in terms of investors there are still way too few who have exposure to Trend filling
claims.claim: Drawdowns in trend following offer entry points because too few investors hold it.
claims.direction: allocate to trend following after drawdown

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: the cost with that of having low correlation is the fact that when there is calm periods in the market such as when uh where we have interest rates have volatility has come down
claims.claim: The cost of crisis alpha and low correlation is poor performance in calm, sideways markets with lower rate and inflation volatility, and investors forget the crisis benefits when rebalancing.
claims.direction: trend following weak in calm markets
claims.testable: yes: performance by vol regime testable

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: currencies have been uh as far as I can tell has been hit pretty hard not least from the the strength the new found strength of the Japanese uh Yen
claims.claim: In July 2024 trend followers suffered reversals across currencies (yen strength), equities, metals, energy and bonds, a transition period.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer closed yesterday at 36 that's weak it's not super weak but it is weak
claims.claim: A Trend barometer of 36 indicates a weak environment and negative month for trend followers.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: St gen CTA index down 2.19% in July up 4.91% uh for the year
claims.claim: In July 2024 trend indices were down about 1.5-2.2% for the month and up about 5-6% YTD; MSCI World up about 10% YTD and the bond index slightly down.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-term Traders; MSCI World; S&P Global Developed Sovereign Bond

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: if let's say a a market has been trading poorly over the last few years that doesn't mean it's going to trade poorly going forward
claims.claim: Do not drop a market from a trend portfolio just because it lost money for years: it may be a diversifier whose future is unknown.
claims.testable: yes: removal rules can be backtested

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: rates are never going to go below zero so therefore uh and if we're getting close to the zero bound let's of course drop that market
claims.claim: Dropping short-term interest rate markets near the zero bound would have been wrong because rates went negative; one-sided-market assumptions fail.
claims.indicator: short-term interest rate futures near zero bound

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: central banks actually intervene because they want to punish speculators
claims.claim: Central-bank-intervention markets (managed FX) that punish speculators justify lower exposure.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: you want to have two-sided markets where you have hedgers and both speculators if it's pure speculative then that could be a a problem
claims.claim: Market selection criteria: two-sided markets with hedgers and speculators; markets with only speculators are a problem.
claims.testable: partly: hedger share via COT data

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: all professional Traders it's going to be harder to make money
claims.claim: Markets with only professional traders (little retail) are harder to make money in.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: the volume starts to fall below a certain threshold or open interest Falls I'd want to drop it out because uh because then then you could get more likely a jump risk which could work against you
claims.claim: Drop markets when volume or open interest fall below minimums, because illiquidity brings jump risk; avoid brand-new markets.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: not so much if it makes money or loses money but how it makes the money and lose the money is it all coming with a single trade
claims.claim: When reviewing a market, check how it earned (one trade or many, choppiness) rather than whether it made money.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there you have to have some safeguards some volatility flaws that you know doesn't prevent you is the word I'm looking for here prevents you from sizing up and and getting really badly hurt
claims.claim: Use volatility floors and multiple lookbacks so that suppressed volatility (Swiss franc, short rates) does not lead to oversized positions.
claims.testable: yes: vol-floor effect can be backtested

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Coco literally was not profitable as far as I can tell for the last 15 or 20 years prior to the beginning of January 2023
claims.claim: Cocoa was unprofitable for trend followers for 15-20 years and then turned extremely profitable in 2023-24, so removing markets for past losses is dangerous.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there's nothing wrong with having a market that doesn't really make money for you if it makes money when a lot of other things is not making money for you in your portfolio
claims.claim: A market that makes little money but pays when others lose still adds diversification value.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: it underperformed relative to a lot of ctas who did have Coco
claims.claim: An index excluding cocoa (Credit Suisse managed futures index) underperformed CTAs that held cocoa; few markets are dropped except for liquidity.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: I will increase my exposure in those markets that have low volatility and then if let's say there is a spike in volatility I could be on a wrong wrong-sided on that market
claims.claim: Volatility targeting increases size when volatility is artificially low (Swiss franc peg), which was the worst action when the peg broke.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: I've never seen a bad back test in terms of performance and sharp
claims.claim: Backtests are valuable not for performance or Sharpe (all look good) but for insight into the manager's care in research and treatment of transaction costs and realism.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: you get insight into the manager in terms of how careful he is with his uh with his research how careful he is at being able to account for all of the realism in the market
claims.claim: Due diligence should ask about backtest assumptions and costs to judge the manager's rigour.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: how does someone build a system not a model and there's a difference between the two I can always come up with a good model
claims.claim: Anyone can build a good model; what matters is applying it across many markets, building portfolios and a full system.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: you have to take off your scientist hat you have to put on the hat of an engineer and then you have to say I am building a factory
claims.claim: Move from backtest (laboratory) to factory: inputs, outputs, timing, costs, and execution must be realistic.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: I would say it's the process of how you do your research which is more important than the actual numbers you generate
claims.claim: Investors' Sharpe thresholds conflict (one rejects below 2, another above 1.25), so research process matters more than the numbers.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: any portfolio you build has to be related to three components one what is the process for return generation two what is the portfolio construction and what is the risk management
claims.claim: Evaluate systematic managers by return generation, portfolio construction and risk management.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: if it's more regression based or it's model based then there's a potential for parameter un uh instability in some sense you you actually like simple rules
claims.claim: Regression or model-based signals risk parameter instability, so simple rules are preferred.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: that's where you're getting the only free lunch available in finance which is diversification
claims.claim: Portfolio construction (diversification) is the one free lunch available.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: a good model should incorporate uh risk management in the portfolio construction and decision rules that you determine when to get long but then you also have a uh determination of when to exit
claims.claim: Risk management belongs in the model's entry and exit rules, with a stop loss as a fail-safe protecting investor principal.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: perhaps the best way to approach it is to look at this from a trend following perspective and let the prices themselves tell you what you should do
claims.claim: When valuation and the rate outlook give compelling reasons for both stocks and bonds, follow price trends instead.
claims.direction: follow trend in stocks and bonds

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: if correlations change on you and if correlation especially if you have the classic 6040 portfolio it turns positive is is that you're really going to get a lot more volatility in your overall portfolio
claims.claim: If stock-bond correlation turns positive, 60/40 volatility rises and bonds lose their diversification role, so risk should be monitored via the off-diagonal covariance terms.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the one-year rolling correlation is actually at the highest it's been in a very very long time
claims.claim: The one-year rolling stock-bond correlation was at a multi-year high in mid-2024, exposing portfolios to higher risk.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: to really start to think about valuation because uh then it's a relative return situation not a diversification question
claims.claim: When stock-bond correlation is positive, bonds are no longer diversifiers and the choice becomes relative valuation.
claims.indicator: relative valuation of stocks vs bonds

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: there's loss mitigation strategies equity diversifiers and we'll call Equity complements and Equity substitutes
claims.claim: GIC/JPMorgan paper classifies hedge fund strategies into loss mitigation, equity diversifiers, equity complements and equity substitutes.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: one you want to look at what's the correlation with equities
claims.claim: Classify strategies by equity correlation, drawdown mitigation relative to equities, and alpha after beta.
claims.indicator: correlation to equities, relative drawdown, alpha

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: lo and behold bage Futures is probably number two number one was uh was a global ma Global macro
claims.claim: In the GIC/JPM framework managed futures ranked second for alpha after beta and global macro first.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: if you look at what is the strategy that seems to fit within that it's probably Trend following on all three of those counts
claims.claim: Trend following meets all three criteria (low equity correlation, drawdown mitigation, positive alpha); not an equity substitute.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: we often use judgment that's you know wedded in a specific model or school of thought
claims.claim: Being wedded to one model produces false alarms, e.g. post-GFC QE did not cause rampant inflation; entertain alternatives.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: we have a lot of of of macroeconomists or are doomsday or is is they they they make their bones by uh by suggesting that the world is going to come to an end
claims.claim: Doomsday macro forecasts are often wrong; Covid saw a sharp drop but a fast recovery, better than expected.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: prices are Primal and use prices as your sort of your null hypothesis
claims.claim: Use prices as the null hypothesis and let prices speak before departing.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: what's the price action that you see in markets in the next couple of days and that's going to be what the real driver
claims.claim: Don't chase data releases such as PCE; the price reaction to the data is what drives positions.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: they looked at llm large language model uh models and they tied it to time series
claims.claim: A paper found LLMs add little to time series forecasting, so model building is harder than expected.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: she learning does pretty well during up parts of the business cycle but then when you hit the down uh the downdraft when you hit a recession
claims.claim: Machine learning performs well in expansions but poorly in recessions because training data has few recession periods.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: people were quick to to kind of state that this would have a negative impact on Trend following
claims.claim: Every technology wave in 30 years was predicted to hurt trend following, and it has not.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: the purpose of building models is to take public information which could be past prices or macro data and then we want to turn it into private information
claims.claim: Prices are public and discounted rapidly, so models and new techniques are valuable only if they turn the same public data into private insight others do not have.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: the answer is not going to be digital like like we just need to switch and it's an onoff switch that we should go from one set of models to a new set of models
claims.claim: Adopting new techniques should be gradual, not a binary switch from old to new models.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: we often extrapolate from a small sample on what we might think what will happen in the in the future as opposed to using a very large sample
claims.claim: Law of small numbers: extrapolating from small samples, which affects trend and quant models that decide on limited data, so check sample size and distribution.

claims.speaker: Mark rinsky
claims.quote: if you know the distribution then you probably you're always going to be a uh a mean reverter if you don't know the distribution then you might sort of follow the hot hand
claims.claim: Gambler's fallacy and hot hand: knowing the distribution implies mean reversion, not knowing it implies following the hot hand.
